lessons.title: Direct proportion to a variable (Extended)
lessons.summary: Translate direct proportion into an equation, determine the multiplier and use it to find another value.
lessons.objective: Translate direct proportion into an equation, determine the multiplier and use it to find another value.
lessons.before: Find a ratio and divide to undo multiplication. Use positive values for the practice in this chapter.
lessons.ideas:
\(y\propto x\) gives \(y=kx\). Use one non-zero input and its output to find \(k=\frac yx\).

For a new \(x\), multiply by \(k\). For a new \(y\), divide by \(k\). For positive values, a scale factor on \(x\) acts unchanged on \(y\).

Calculate the output divided by the input for more than one pair. The same ratio should result each time.
lessons.method:
What does the proportional symbol tell us?

The symbol \(\propto\) says there is a fixed multiplying relationship. It is not an equals sign.

How can I work backwards or predict a scale change?

The same \(k\) is used for every related pair. Choose whether the new question gives the input or the output.

How do I know a table fits the direct model?

Direct proportion to \(x\) gives a graph through the origin when zero is included. The table can check the same fact at non-zero inputs.
mistakes: Finding a multiplier means dividing by the input. Taking the difference between the numbers gives a different relationship.
Using the new pair to change the multiplier would define a different model.
Two increasing quantities need not be directly proportional. If the ratio varies, this model does not fit.

examples.title: Find the constant of proportionality
examples.question: \(y\) is directly proportional to \(x\). When \(x=2\), \(y=8\). Find the positive constant of proportionality \(k\) in \(y=k\,x\).
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto x\) mean \(y=k\,x\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=2\) and \(y=8\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{8}{2}=4\).

The model is \(y=4\,x\).

examples.title: Work backwards to a new input
examples.question: \(y\) is directly proportional to \(x\). When \(x=12\), \(y=120\). Find the positive value of \(x\) when \(y=140\). Give an exact answer.
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto x\) mean \(y=k\,x\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=12\) and \(y=120\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{120}{12}=10\).

Rearrange to isolate the transformed input. \(x=\frac{140}{10}=14\).

Undo the transformation to find the positive input. \(x=14\).

examples.title: Recognise the correct equation
examples.question:
\(y\) is directly proportional to \(x\). When \(x=9\), \(y=\frac{171}{5}\). Which equation uses the right type of proportion and the value of \(k\) from the pair?

A. \(y=\frac{19}{5}\,x\)   B. \(y=\frac{19}{5\,x}\)   C. \(y=x+\frac{19}{5}\)   D. \(y=\frac{24}{5}\,x\)
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto x\) mean \(y=k\,x\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=9\) and \(y=\frac{171}{5}\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{171}{5}\div 9=\frac{19}{5}\).

Substitute the value of \(k\) into the matching model. \(y=\frac{19}{5}\,x\).

lessons.title: Inverse proportion to a variable (Extended)
lessons.summary: Recognise a fixed product, calculate the constant and predict the effect of changing a positive input.
lessons.objective: Recognise a fixed product, calculate the constant and predict the effect of changing a positive input.
lessons.before: Recall that a reciprocal is one divided by a value. Division by zero is undefined.
lessons.ideas:
\(y\propto\frac1x\) gives \(y=\frac{k}{x}\). Multiplying by \(x\) shows that \(xy=k\).

If \(x\) is multiplied by a factor \(c\), \(y\) is divided by \(c\). When finding \(x\) from a given \(y\), use \(x=\frac ky\).

Test the same quantity with two supplied pairs. If the products match, use that value of \(k\) in the inverse equation.
lessons.method:
Which part stays constant in inverse proportion?

In an inverse model with positive values, one quantity falls as the other rises. The product stays fixed.

How does the new factor affect the output?

The same value of \(k\) connects every pair. A bigger denominator divides the constant into smaller values.

How do I distinguish a fixed product from a fixed ratio?

Direct proportion to x keeps the output-to-input ratio fixed. Inverse proportion to x keeps the product fixed.
mistakes: Dividing the observed y by x gives a direct-model multiplier. For inverse proportion to x use their product.
Doubling the input would halve the output. Adding or subtracting a fixed amount does not describe the scaling rule.
One decreasing pair of readings is only a hint. Check the products when several pairs are available.

examples.title: Find the constant of proportionality
examples.question: \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x\). When \(x=2\), \(y=2\). Find the positive constant of proportionality \(k\) in \(y=\frac{k}{x}\).
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{x}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{x}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=2\) and \(y=2\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=2\times2=4\).

The model is \(y=\frac{4}{x}\).

examples.title: Work backwards to a new input
examples.question: \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x\). When \(x=12\), \(y=\frac{5}{6}\). Find the positive value of \(x\) when \(y=\frac{5}{7}\). Give an exact answer.
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{x}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{x}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=12\) and \(y=\frac{5}{6}\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{5}{6}\times12=10\).

Rearrange to isolate the transformed input. \(x=10\div \frac{5}{7}=14\).

Undo the transformation to find the positive input. \(x=14\).

examples.title: Recognise the correct equation
examples.question:
\(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x\). When \(x=9\), \(y=\frac{19}{45}\). Which equation uses the right type of proportion and the value of \(k\) from the pair?

A. \(y=\frac{19}{5\,x}\)   B. \(y=\frac{19}{5}\,x\)   C. \(y=x+\frac{19}{5}\)   D. \(y=\frac{24}{5\,x}\)
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{x}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{x}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=9\) and \(y=\frac{19}{45}\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{19}{45}\times9=\frac{19}{5}\).

Substitute the value of \(k\) into the matching model. \(y=\frac{19}{5\,x}\).

lessons.title: Direct proportion to a square or cube (Extended)
lessons.summary: Square or cube the input before using the constant, and reverse the transformation to find a positive input.
lessons.objective: Square or cube the input before using the constant, and reverse the transformation to find a positive input.
lessons.before: Know how a square and a cube change when a positive length is scaled.
lessons.ideas:
Write \(y=kx^2\) for direct proportion to the square and \(y=kx^3\) for the cube. First work out the power of the known input, then divide the known output by it.

In a square model, first isolate and take the positive square root of \(x^2\). In a cube model, take the cube root after finding \(x^3\). If the problem specifies a bracket such as \((x+1)^2\), take the root before subtracting 1. For unshifted powers, doubling x gives factors 4 and 8.

Use the ratio \(\frac{y}{x^2}\) or \(\frac{y}{x^3}\) for each pair. The constancy of the relevant ratio is the check.
lessons.method:
What exactly gets squared or cubed?

Read the power in the relationship before using the pair. A comparable shape may scale by a power of its length.

How can I reverse the model or check a scale factor?

Before taking a root, isolate the expression in \(x\). Use the positive value of \(x\) in the measurement contexts on this page.

How do I test a proposed equation against data?

A successful equation uses the right power of \(x\) and the same numerical coefficient for all pairs.
mistakes: Putting the constant inside the power would raise the constant to that power as well.
The computed square or cube is not necessarily x itself.
The curve need not be straight. The input power, not the plain input, is proportional to y.

examples.title: Find the constant of proportionality
examples.question: \(y\) is directly proportional to the square of \(x\). When \(x=2\), \(y=16\). Find the positive constant of proportionality \(k\) in \(y=k\,x^2\).
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto x^2\) mean \(y=k\,x^2\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=2\) and \(y=16\). \(\left(2\right)^2=4\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{16}{4}=4\).

The model is \(y=4\,x^2\).

examples.title: Work backwards to a new input
examples.question: \(y\) is directly proportional to the square of \(x+1\). Take \(x>-1\). When \(x=11\), \(y=1440\). Find the positive value of \(x\) when \(y=1960\). Give an exact answer.
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \left(x+1\right)^2\) mean \(y=k\,\left(x+1\right)^2\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=11\) and \(y=1440\). \(\left(11+1\right)^2=144\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{1440}{144}=10\).

Rearrange to isolate the transformed input. \(\left(x+1\right)^2=\frac{1960}{10}=196\).

Undo the power or root to isolate \(x+1\), then undo its constant shift. \(x=13\).

examples.title: Recognise the correct equation
examples.question:
\(y\) is directly proportional to the square of \(x\). When \(x=9\), \(y=\frac{1539}{5}\). Which equation uses the right type of proportion and the value of \(k\) from the pair?

A. \(y=\frac{19}{5}\,x^2\)   B. \(y=\frac{19}{5\,x^2}\)   C. \(y=x^2+\frac{19}{5}\)   D. \(y=\frac{24}{5}\,x^2\)
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto x^2\) mean \(y=k\,x^2\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=9\) and \(y=\frac{1539}{5}\). \(\left(9\right)^2=81\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{1539}{5}\div 81=\frac{19}{5}\).

Substitute the value of \(k\) into the matching model. \(y=\frac{19}{5}\,x^2\).

lessons.title: Inverse proportion to a square or cube (Extended)
lessons.summary: Use a positive squared or cubed denominator, recover the constant and compare the size of a model’s outputs.
lessons.objective: Use a positive squared or cubed denominator, recover the constant and compare the size of a model’s outputs.
lessons.before: Find the square or cube of a positive number and take a reciprocal.
lessons.ideas:
Use \(y=\frac{k}{x^2}\) for an inverse square and \(y=\frac{k}{x^3}\) for an inverse cube. Multiply the known output by the relevant power of the known input to find k.

For unshifted powers, doubling the input divides inverse-square output by 4 and inverse-cube output by 8. When recovering \(x\), isolate the whole denominator and undo the power.

Check \(yx^2\) or \(yx^3\) across known pairs. With \(y=\frac{k}{(x-2)^2}\), the fixed product is \(y(x-2)^2\).
lessons.method:
Which expression belongs in the denominator?

The output is proportional to the reciprocal of the stated power. Evaluate the power before dividing.

What happens if the input changes by a known factor?

The change acts on the denominator. First apply the power to the input scale factor.

Which product stays fixed?

The product of the output and the correct input power should equal the fitted constant.
mistakes: The model uses a reciprocal power, not a negative output. The output stays positive on the positive branch.
Taking the reciprocal before or after the correct power leads to the same factor. Omitting the power altogether does not.
Testing \(xy\) for an inverse square can make a correct table look incorrect.

examples.title: Find the constant of proportionality
examples.question: \(y\) is inversely proportional to the square of \(x\). When \(x=2\), \(y=1\). Find the positive constant of proportionality \(k\) in \(y=\frac{k}{x^2}\).
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{x^2}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{x^2}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=2\) and \(y=1\). \(\left(2\right)^2=4\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=1\times4=4\).

The model is \(y=\frac{4}{x^2}\).

examples.title: Work backwards to a new input
examples.question: \(y\) is inversely proportional to the square of \(x-2\). Take \(x>2\). When \(x=14\), \(y=\frac{5}{72}\). Find the positive value of \(x\) when \(y=\frac{5}{98}\). Give an exact answer.
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{\left(x-2\right)^2}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{\left(x-2\right)^2}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=14\) and \(y=\frac{5}{72}\). \(\left(14-2\right)^2=144\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{5}{72}\times144=10\).

Rearrange to isolate the transformed input. \(\left(x-2\right)^2=10\div \frac{5}{98}=196\).

Undo the power or root to isolate \(x-2\), then undo its constant shift. \(x=16\).

examples.title: Recognise the correct equation
examples.question:
\(y\) is inversely proportional to the square of \(x\). When \(x=9\), \(y=\frac{19}{405}\). Which equation uses the right type of proportion and the value of \(k\) from the pair?

A. \(y=\frac{19}{5\,x^2}\)   B. \(y=\frac{19}{5}\,x^2\)   C. \(y=x^2+\frac{19}{5}\)   D. \(y=\frac{24}{5\,x^2}\)
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{x^2}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{x^2}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=9\) and \(y=\frac{19}{405}\). \(\left(9\right)^2=81\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{19}{405}\times81=\frac{19}{5}\).

Substitute the value of \(k\) into the matching model. \(y=\frac{19}{5\,x^2}\).

lessons.title: Direct and inverse square-root proportion (Extended)
lessons.summary: Apply the square-root relationship in both directions and square a transformed value to recover the original input.
lessons.objective: Apply the square-root relationship in both directions and square a transformed value to recover the original input.
lessons.before: Read the principal square root of a positive number, including a perfect-square fraction.
lessons.ideas:
Write \(y=k\sqrt{x}\). From a known pair, divide y by the square root of x. Use that same k with the new square root. If the root covers \(x+1\), add 1 before taking the root.

Write \(y=\frac{k}{\sqrt{x}}\). Find \(k=y\sqrt{x}\). To work back from y, find \(\sqrt{x}=\frac ky\) and square that value. For a root over \(x-2\), add 2 only after squaring.

Calculate the root before completing the ratio or product. Compare the new output with the original to check which direction it changed.
lessons.method:
How do I find the constant in a direct square-root model?

A directly proportional output tracks the root of the input instead of the input itself. The root symbol here means the positive square root of the given positive value.

What changes when the root is in the denominator?

The positive square root is used again. In this case the root is the denominator, and division by that value changes the direction.

How can I compare a direct root, an inverse root and a square?

The word ‘root’ means the input factor gets smaller when it is greater than 1. Inverse proportion then takes the reciprocal of that transformed factor.
mistakes: Do not square the input or take the square root of the whole output equation before isolating the correct quantity.
Finding the square root of \(k/y\) reverses the wrong operation. That quotient already represents the square root of x.
The square and the square root of the same scale factor are usually very different numbers.

examples.title: Find the constant of proportionality
examples.question: \(y\) is directly proportional to the square root of \(x\). When \(x=4\), \(y=8\). Find the positive constant of proportionality \(k\) in \(y=k\,\sqrt{x}\).
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \sqrt{x}\) mean \(y=k\,\sqrt{x}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=4\) and \(y=8\). \(\sqrt{4}=2\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{8}{2}=4\).

The model is \(y=4\,\sqrt{x}\).

examples.title: Predict a new output
examples.question: \(y\) is inversely proportional to the square root of \(x\). When \(x=144\), \(y=\frac{5}{6}\). Find \(y\) when \(x=196\). Give an exact answer.
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{\sqrt{x}}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=144\) and \(y=\frac{5}{6}\). \(\sqrt{144}=12\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{5}{6}\times12=10\).

\(y=\frac{10}{\sqrt{196}}=\frac{5}{7}\).

The exact output is \(\frac{5}{7}\).

examples.title: Use a scale factor to predict the change
examples.question: \(y\) is directly proportional to the square root of \(x\). The initial pair is \(x=81\) and \(y=\frac{171}{5}\). The value of \(x\) is then multiplied by \(36\). By what factor is \(y\) multiplied?
examples.solution:
The factor applying to the transformed input is \(\sqrt{36}=6\).

The transformed input is multiplied by a constant, so the same factor applies to the output.

The resulting scale factor for \(y\) is \(6\).

lessons.title: Direct and inverse cube-root proportion (Extended)
lessons.summary: Use the cube-root multiplier or divisor, recover positive inputs and connect volume scaling to length scaling.
lessons.objective: Use the cube-root multiplier or divisor, recover positive inputs and connect volume scaling to length scaling.
lessons.before: Find the cube root of a perfect cube, and reverse a cube root by cubing.
lessons.ideas:
Write \(y=k\sqrt[3]{x}\). Use the cube root of the known input before dividing the output by it to find the constant.

Write \(y=\frac{k}{\sqrt[3]{x}}\). Multiply the known output by the cube root to get k. If y is supplied, first find \(\sqrt[3]{x}=\frac ky\), then cube.

A factor of \(\frac{1}{8}\) on x gives a direct cube-root factor of \(\frac{1}{2}\) and an inverse cube-root factor of \(2\).
lessons.method:
Why does a length sometimes depend on a cube root?

Volumes of similar shapes scale with the cube of the length scale. Reversing that relation brings in a cube root.

What if the cube root is in the denominator?

An inverse cube-root model uses the same transformed input, but the output divides the constant by that value.

How can I check that the order of operations makes sense?

Read what is under the root, or in the denominator, before applying the constant. Think about the direction and rough size before doing the arithmetic.
mistakes: The small 3 on the root sign names a cube root. It does not multiply a square root.
Taking an ordinary reciprocal of x treats the model as inverse linear and ignores the cube root.
The reciprocal relationship does not make the output negative.

examples.title: Find the constant of proportionality
examples.question: \(y\) is directly proportional to the cube root of \(x\). When \(x=8\), \(y=8\). Find the positive constant of proportionality \(k\) in \(y=k\,\sqrt[3]{x}\).
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \sqrt[3]{x}\) mean \(y=k\,\sqrt[3]{x}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=8\) and \(y=8\). \(\sqrt[3]{8}=2\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{8}{2}=4\).

The model is \(y=4\,\sqrt[3]{x}\).

examples.title: Predict a new output
examples.question: \(y\) is inversely proportional to the cube root of \(x\). When \(x=1728\), \(y=\frac{5}{6}\). Find \(y\) when \(x=2744\). Give an exact answer.
examples.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{x}}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{\sqrt[3]{x}}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=1728\) and \(y=\frac{5}{6}\). \(\sqrt[3]{1728}=12\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{5}{6}\times12=10\).

\(y=\frac{10}{\sqrt[3]{2744}}=\frac{5}{7}\).

The exact output is \(\frac{5}{7}\).

examples.title: Use a scale factor to predict the change
examples.question: \(y\) is directly proportional to the cube root of \(x\). The initial pair is \(x=729\) and \(y=\frac{171}{5}\). The value of \(x\) is then multiplied by \(216\). By what factor is \(y\) multiplied?
examples.solution:
The factor applying to the transformed input is \(\sqrt[3]{216}=6\).

The transformed input is multiplied by a constant, so the same factor applies to the output.

The resulting scale factor for \(y\) is \(6\).

\(y\) is inversely proportional to the square root of \(x-2\). Take \(x>2\). All values of \(x\) and \(y\) are positive. When \(x=51\), \(y=\frac{33}{35}\).

  1. Write an equation for \(y\) in terms of \(x\).

    [2]

  2. Find \(x\) when \(y=\frac{33}{20}\). Give an exact answer.

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{x-2}}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{\sqrt{x-2}}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=51\) and \(y=\frac{33}{35}\). \(\sqrt{51-2}=7\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{33}{35}\times7=\frac{33}{5}\).

The equation is \(y=\frac{33}{5\,\sqrt{x-2}}\).

(b)

Use the same relationship. \(y=\frac{33}{5\,\sqrt{x-2}}\).

When \(y=\frac{33}{20}\), the transformed input must equal \(4\).

Undo the transformation and subtract the inside offset. \(x=18\).

\(y\) is directly proportional to the cube root of \(x+1\). Take \(x>-1\). All values of \(x\) and \(y\) are positive. When \(x=63\), \(y=\frac{140}{3}\).

  1. Write an equation for \(y\) in terms of \(x\).

    [2]

  2. Find \(x\) when \(y=\frac{175}{3}\). Give an exact answer.

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

The symbols \(y\propto \sqrt[3]{x+1}\) mean \(y=k\,\sqrt[3]{x+1}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=63\) and \(y=\frac{140}{3}\). \(\sqrt[3]{63+1}=4\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{140}{3}\div 4=\frac{35}{3}\).

The equation is \(y=\frac{35}{3}\,\sqrt[3]{x+1}\).

(b)

Use the same relationship. \(y=\frac{35}{3}\,\sqrt[3]{x+1}\).

When \(y=\frac{175}{3}\), the transformed input must equal \(5\).

Undo the transformation and subtract the inside offset. \(x=124\).

questions.title: Model proportional data and check a scale factor
questions.prompt_html:
A scale calculation links the volume \(x\) of a similar object and the ratio \(y\) of a reference length to one of its dimensions. \(y\) is inversely proportional to the cube root of \(x\). All values of \(x\) and \(y\) are positive. When \(x=729\), \(y=2\).

  1. Write an equation for \(y\) in terms of \(x\).

    [2]

  2. Find \(y\) when \(x=2744\). Give an exact answer.

    [2]

  3. Starting anywhere in this positive model, \(x\) is multiplied by \(\frac{2744}{729}\). What is the resulting scale factor for \(y\)?

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{x}}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{\sqrt[3]{x}}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=729\) and \(y=2\). \(\sqrt[3]{729}=9\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=2\times9=18\).

The equation is \(y=\frac{18}{\sqrt[3]{x}}\).

(b)

Use the same equation with \(x=2744\).

\(y=\frac{18}{\sqrt[3]{2744}}=\frac{9}{7}\).

(c)

The transformed input scales by \(\sqrt[3]{\frac{2744}{729}}=\frac{14}{9}\).

It is in the denominator, so \(y\) scales by the reciprocal.

The resulting factor is \(\frac{9}{14}\).
